limitations: ODM is implemented and dispatcher-tested (mocks + stub engine end-to-end export), but ODM was NOT exercised against the REAL engine in H02; real-engine diagnostic smoke covers RunAccessibility only.
The real-engine diagnostic run uses NUMBA_DISABLE_JIT=1 for speed; such records are structurally non-qualifying (measurement_class=diagnostic_source) and timings are not comparable to JIT runs.

inspect_thread_pools output is recorded in every ready/job record but no test asserts numba-specific values (the stub arm has no numba; effective counts are honest Nones there). Arrow and turn/cluster pools are captured indirectly via full Settings echo, not by dedicated inspection.

The worker-side stuck-result-channel path (_put_message deadline then exit 73) is implemented but never triggered by a test; bounded-queue deadlock-freedom is proven structurally (bounded maxsize + interleaved draining) and by the slow_drain full-input-queue run.
Warm-up hash-then-discard is implemented and recorded (warmup_ns, warmup file hashes); no dedicated test asserts the warmup record fields.

The flow worst-case admission gate W*(H+K)<=C is scoped to analysis=flow in batch mode: AggregateFlow's stripe executor only exists for flow runs; accessibility/ODM would otherwise be refused by the production-default stripe estimate (cpu_count-1) that they never spawn. Recorded in admission as flow_worst_case_gate.
On macOS, USS/PSS are denied to non-root (AccessDenied): the sampler falls back to plain RSS for those processes instead of dropping them (implemented + labelled); on Linux USS/PSS are recorded.
cold_process_ns compile-cold semantics require the operator to designate a NEW --cache-root for the cold test; the harness never wipes caches.

identity_sha256 is a canonical-JSON integrity hash, not a keyed signature: tampering requires re-signing, which the tree/module-hash and dist-info guards then catch against disk; arms are trusted to the extent the campaign controls identity generation.

Installed-mode guards were validated against a physically laid-out stub venv (package + dist-info inside a synthetic site-packages), not against a real built wheel; W00 (build wheels + installed execution proof) is the task that exercises a real wheel.
